chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'Does the raj'ah (return of the wife to the husband during the waiting period) occur without sexual intercourse?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: Raj'ah: The act of a husband taking back his wife during the 'iddah' period after a revocable divorce.
key_terms.جِمَاعٍ: Jima': Sexual intercourse or consummation of marriage.

ai.seo_question: Does a husband need to have sexual intercourse with his wife to validly take her back during the divorce waiting period (raj'ah)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), the concept of *raj'ah* is clarified as a unilateral right of the husband to restore the marital bond during the *iddah* without requiring a new contract or consummation. This ruling underscores the revocable nature of the first and second divorces in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the legal act of return from the physical act of intercourse. It highlights that the marital tie remains intact, allowing the husband to resume cohabitation simply by intent and declaration.
